label: first copy step (echoed first token) in long sequences starting with s/w/e/m and with h/j/n early
explanation: Sparse feature; 94% of activation mass is at recall_idx==1 (the step right after <DEL>, where the input is the echoed first token and the output is original token 1), and 80% of it is in sequences with L>=8 (L=9 gives ~58%). Within that context it fires on only ~1% of steps. It is strongly selective for the content: first token s, w or e (also m) and h/j/n among the next few original tokens (next_out h is 15x lift). The top examples look like s u n h..., s y h h..., w k h j..., e h h v n j.... Magnitude rises with L and with these token matches; it seems to be a soft threshold over sequence content that no clean boolean captures. Small leftovers: the <DEL> step (1%), recall_idx 2 (2%), and original step t=2 (2%). It does not fire in the original phase in general, or late in the copy phase. Best dev F1 is only 0.23 (P 0.16, R 0.42); the predicate (recall_idx==1)&(L>=8) alone covers 80% of the mass at 1% precision.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=2 & prev_tok=o (+7.06), t=2 & in_tok=i (+5.19), in_tok=s (+4.84), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=w (+4.03), orig0=e (+3.31), orig4=o (+3.13). Lower it: in_tok=j (-3.15), out_tok=c (-2.85), orig1=l (-2.77), orig1=a (-2.54).
